correctness.rationale: Chari–Joswig gives the full nonequivariant free homology concentration. The two alternating formal simplex boundaries have disjoint primitive facet coefficients and span the integral top cycle lattice; rotation acts on each by the parity of an n-cycle, and reflection exchanges them. A generator rotation fixes no nonempty simplex, hence reduced Lefschetz number -1; a reflection fixes two disjoint simplices geometrically and has reduced Lefschetz number 1. Because the top reflection trace vanishes, these force both generators to act trivially on the rank-one H2. Independent exact checks enumerated n=5..11 signed traces and n=5..9 augmented-chain ranks in two fields. No finite enumeration is substituted for the universal proof.
risks: The homotopy rank theorem is correctly cited as a prior premise, not independently reproved here.

value.rationale: Cycles have an intrinsic dihedral symmetry and their pure Morse complexes are a foundational infinite family. The top integral lattice and its parity-dependent rotation twist are strictly stronger than the previously known ranks: a rank-two rational character does not specify the integral lattice, and a wedge decomposition without equivariance does not determine the group action. The degree-two invariant and rational quotient consequence make the representation structurally useful. The result is neither an arbitrary parameter slice nor a recomputation of sphere counts.
risks: No generalization beyond cycles or integral quotient-torsion theorem is asserted.
